description: FLAC3D is commercial three-dimensional continuum software for geomechanics from Itasca Consulting Group, based on the explicit finite-difference method. It analyses soil, rock, concrete and structural ground support, with groundwater flow and thermal calculations, dynamic analysis of earthquakes and liquefaction, and 26 built-in constitutive models plus user-defined ones. The vendor lists civil applications (caverns, dams, retaining structures, foundations, tunnels and shafts, slopes and embankments), energy applications (CO2 storage, fault stability, induced seismicity, nuclear waste isolation, salt caverns, underground infrastructure, wellbores) and mining applications (blasting, crown and underground pillars, open pit walls, solution mining, stopes, tailings dams and stockpiles). Models are built in a GUI with sketch, slope and tunnel wizards and octree meshing, and scripted with the FISH language and Python; data can be imported from MINEDW and RockMass Technologies hardware. It is sold under commercial licences (USB key or web licence, two instances per computer) with documentation, tutorials and training. Caveats: it is proprietary and every model is site specific, so no public model library comes with it. For simulation it gives physical models of the stability and failure of tailings dams, pit slopes, tunnels and foundations for fragility, hazard and resilience analysis of mining and civil infrastructure. Related catalogue records include the Mount Polley breach investigation and the Global Tailings Portal.
